data.cause: The provider side stopped carrying traffic at ~02:01 (cable modem logged "No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out"); the modem re-registered and now reports OPERATIONAL, but the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 still does not answer ARP, so gw.lan's valid WAN lease and default route lead to a dead upstream path.
evidence: arp -a -n: '?(198.51.100.1) at (incomplete) on vtnet0 expired' — no L2 reachability to the ISP next hop, while LAN neighbours resolve normally
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1: 100% loss with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available'; ping -c 3 -n 10.20.0.9 succeeds 3/3, so the firewall's own stack and LAN are fine

cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0: lease for 198.51.100.27/24, router 198.51.100.1, lease valid until 2026/3/6 — WAN config/lease is not the problem; netstat -rn shows the default route via 198.51.100.1 present
tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' (matches outage start ~02:01), then 02:28:21 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete'

tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: status OPERATIONAL at 03:00 and 03:30, min_snr 37.7-37.8 dB, modem uptime rising — the cable access link itself has recovered, yet traffic still does not get out

tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: reloads at 02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25 all returned rc=0 but the outage continued; 03:30 decision 'action: none, reason: reload_cap, reloads_24h: 12, max_reloads_24h: 12' — a further WAN reload is both blocked by the cap and already proven ineffective

dmesg -a: repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' with link DOWN/UP flaps during the outage window, while netstat -m shows 0 mbuf requests denied — stalls were on the upstream path, not firewall resource exhaustion
data.recommendation: Report an outage to the ISP for the circuit on gw.lan's WAN (modem re-registered and shows OPERATIONAL since 02:28, but their gateway 198.51.100.1 gives no ARP reply and drops all traffic). Nothing on gw.lan needs changing: the lease and default route are valid, and four WAN reloads already had no effect. Do not run another wan_reload now — it would only add a fifth ineffective reload against a 12-per-24h cap that is already reached. Keep the watchdog in its current state, let the existing lease stand, and open a ticket with the provider; re-check reachability of 198.51.100.1 once they respond.
data.detail: ISP next hop unreachable (no ARP reply for 198.51.100.1) despite modem re-registration
